mechanism_narrative: A persistently low federal funds rate (below 0.5%) indicates an accommodative monetary policy that reduces the cost of capital for corporations, leading to higher equity valuations and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate below 9.0% over a 3-month window signals strengthening labor market conditions, which typically precedes increased corporate hiring and higher consumer spending, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE falls below 9.0% within 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) above their 3-month moving averages indicates robust consumer demand and business investment, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when both HOUST and RSAFS are above their 3-month moving averages.

mechanism_narrative: In a period of rising industrial production (INDPRO above 100.5), the manufacturing sector's expansion signals improving corporate earnings prospects, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO > 100.5.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the annual inflation rate above 2.5% (as measured by CPIAUCSL) signals potential monetary tightening, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL rises above 2.5% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous decline in unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 9.5% and positive growth in employment (PAYEMS) above 0.5% over 3 months indicates a strong labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 9.5% and PAYEMS growth > 0.5% in 3 months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE < 9.5% and PAYEMS growth > 0.5% over 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in housing starts (HOUST) above 580.0 thousand units signals strong residential construction activity, which typically precedes increased consumer spending and corporate investment, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when HOUST rises above 580.0.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 99.5 indicates a contraction in manufacturing output, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO falls below 99.5.
